title: Regulatory-aware A/B + Canary Gating for Private Deployments (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft to define a lightweight, repeatable gating protocol for running A/B tests and canaries inside Private/VPC deployments where regulatory controls (data residency, auditability, KMS/HSM, data minimization) matter. Aim is to give PMs, SREs, Legal, and Solutions a common checklist and telemetry contract to avoid late-stage compliance blockers during rollouts.

Audience and scope:
- Primary: product managers shipping model changes or feature flags into customer Private deployments; solutions engineers configuring experiments; SRE and security reviewers.
- Scope: behavioral and model-level A/B variants, staged canaries, traffic-slice experiments executed inside customer-managed VPCs or on-prem packages. Not covering Hosted API experiments.
- Non-goals: detailed legal language for contracts; deep data export policies (these live in CONF-4521).

High-level risk model (why this exists):
- Private deployments often mean customer data never leaves their network, but our A/B tooling may still need control-plane coordination, telemetry, or SDK hooks that touch telemetry or leak metadata.
- Regulators & customers require auditable approvals and proof that experiments do not exfiltrate PII, do not change retention profiles, and that key management and logging behavior remain intact.
- Failures: experiment accidentally turns on model that stores prompt logs with PHI, telemetry samples user text, or experiment routing bypasses customer-approved model pins.

Regulatory gating principles (condensed):
1) Safety-first: experiments default to zero-data telemetry until explicit signoff.
2) Least privilege: any control-plane signal that references customer data uses hashed/derivative keys only.
3) Explainability: experiment must provide a short plain-English description of what changes, data touched, and rollback strategy.
4) Auditability: all approvals, telemetry sampling rates, and rollout percentages are recorded in the deployment audit log.

Pre-launch checklist (owner: experiment lead / PM):
- Experiment intent doc (one paragraph): what variant does and success metrics.
- Data residency assertion: confirm experiment does not require log export outside the customer's network. If it does, attach signed approval from customer security.
- Telemetry contract: list of telemetry keys used, sampling rates, retention, and whether any raw text leaves the VPC.
- KMS/HSM usage: confirm whether variant requires new keys; if yes, provide key ARN and SC (security contact) signoff.
- Privacy review: email from Privacy/Legal approving the experiment (attach).
- SRE capacity check: estimate RPS and burst model, confirm Dedicated pools or local inference nodes coverage.
- Feature flag plan: exact flag names, default state, canary percentages and escalation thresholds.
- Rollback automation: script or runbook snippet that reverts traffic slices and model pins in <5 minutes.

Design constraints for A/B and canary inside private deployments:
- No raw prompt telemetry by default. Telemetry may only contain derived metrics (token counts, latency, error codes, model id).
- If label or content sampling is required for quality evals, sampling must be opt-in on a per-customer basis and documented in the customer integration ticket.
- All experiment-control messages to agents/clients must not contain identifiers (use hashed user_id only).
- Model variants that change hallucination/knowledge behaviors require an additional evaluation of external data sources used by the variant.

Telemetry contract (minimum required fields):
- experiment_id (string, unique), variant_id (string), sample_rate_pct (integer), metric_buckets: [latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, error_code], model_pin (string), telemetry_destination ("vpc-only" | "control-plane" with signed approval).
- Retention_policy: specify in days and must match customer-approved retention ceilings.
- Any field that could contain user text must be declared 'redactable' and default to true.

Example low-risk canary (pattern):
1) 0% -> 0.5% (synthetic/internal annotated traffic only) for 24 hours; collect metric deltas and logs.
2) 0.5% -> 2% (customer-simulated traffic with anonymization) for 48 hours; additional privacy signoff required.
3) 2% -> 10% gating: legal & customer security must approve, retention policy confirmed.
4) 10% -> 50% only with automated rollback monitors enabled and SRE on-call assigned.

Signal and guardrail matrix (quick):
- Latency: 2x baseline -> auto-scale attempt; if >2x for 15 minutes then rollback slice by 50%.
- Error rate: >1% absolute increase -> immediate pause + page SRE.
- Privacy-violation: any raw-text telemetry seen in control-plane -> immediate full rollback and compliance incident opened.
- Model-behavior degradation (metrics drop vs baseline by >10% on accuracy/relevance) -> halt and notify product lead.

Stakeholder runbook (roles & responsibilities):
- Experiment owner (PM): creates intent doc, coordinates privacy/legal signoff, requests SRE capacity.
- Solutions Eng (pre-launch): validates feature flags, connectivity inside VPC, demonstrates KMS behavior.
- SRE: verifies autoscaling, prepares rollback helpers, defines alert thresholds.
- Legal/Privacy: signs off on telemetry contract and data residency.
- Customer Security (if customer-managed): explicit written approval for any telemetry leaving VPC.

Escalation and post-mortem expectations:
- Any gating violation triggers: immediate rollback, incident ticket, 24-hour triage call.
- Post-mortem: 72-hour draft + 2-week final with action items assigned.

Simulation and dry-run checklist (recommended before first customer-facing canary):
- Run synthetic workload that includes edge-case prompts used by the customer (no real customer data).
- Validate telemetry flows do not contain text fields.
- Test rollback script against a staging VPC; measure rollback time.
- Run load to validate scaling path and cold-start latencies for model pins.

Open questions / items to resolve (working):
- Should we allow hashed prompt snippets as part of the telemetry for quality debugging? Legal leaning: no by default; allow per-customer opt-in.
- Mechanism to prove to customers that no raw prompts were exfiltrated (screenshot of logs + signed hash registry?).
- UX: how do we present gating state in Redwood Console for Private deployments without exposing telemetry?

Next steps (owner: Aisha):
- Iterate this draft with Legal and SREs (target review meeting 2024-11-12).
- Build a one-page template that experiment owners fill out (experimental-intent-template-private.json).
- Add a gated checkbox in Console "requires privacy signoff" that blocks canary percentage increases until approvals are attached.

Notes to self / shorthand: 
- keep default telemetry to "counts & codes"; permit sampled labels only with explicit signed approvals; rollbacks must be scriptable; record all approvals in audit.

-- end of draft --
